treaty_name: Convention between the United Kingdom and Austria for the avoidance of double taxation with respect to taxes on income and on capital gains (2018)
eif_quote: A new convention with Austria was signed on 23 October 2018 and entered into force on 1 March 2019.
source_title: 2018 UK-Austria Double Taxation Convention — in force (gov.uk HTML)

rates.quote: b) shall, notwithstanding the provisions of sub-paragraph a), be exempt from tax in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident if the beneficial owner of the dividends is: (i) a company (other than a partnership) which is a resident of the other Contracting State and controls, directly or indirectly, at least 10 per cent of the voting power in the company paying the dividends (other than where the dividends are paid by a relevant investment vehicle); or (ii) a pension scheme.
the tax so charged shall not exceed: (i) 10 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends, except as provided in sub-paragraph a) (ii);
Interest arising in a Contracting State and beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State.
Royalties arising in a Contracting State and beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding the other provisions of this Convention, a benefit under this Convention shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or a capital gain if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of this Convention.

notes: valid_from = later of the two States' effective dates (Art. 28(1)): Austria from fiscal years beginning 1 Jan 2020; UK from 6 Apr 2019 (income tax) / 1 Apr 2019 (corporation tax). Dividends: 0% also for pension schemes (Art. 10(2)(b)(ii)); 15% where paid by a relevant investment vehicle (Austrian real estate investment fund, UK REIT/PAIF) per Art. 10(2)(a)(ii) and the 0% company tier excludes such vehicles. 10% voting-power test (controls directly or indirectly), no holding period. Not covered by MLI; PPT is in the treaty itself (Art. 27). Replaced the 1969 convention.
